guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers are slightly less aggressive on Ohio State than the market, but the case for Illinois is less about trusting its offense and more about questioning the degree of separation being priced. Illinois faces difficult paths on the ground and in creating scoring opportunities, which could leave its defense on the field without much support.

The biggest concern for us is Ohio State’s passing game against an Illinois pass defense that our metrics view as vulnerable. Julian Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes last season, while Jeremiah Smith entered 2026 with 2,709 career receiving yards and 29 touchdowns. Ohio State also returned 85.8 percent of its qualifying offensive-line snaps, giving that passing attack meaningful continuity.

We are not treating Ohio State’s dominant opener as proof of another runaway result, though its 434 passing yards against Ball State fit the broader matchup concern. Our model sees a small disagreement with the market, but Ohio State has clear advantages on both sides of the ball. For us, that makes the available value too thin, so we pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Ohio State’s passing offense against the Illinois secondary. If Illinois cannot limit efficient early-down completions or prevent explosive gains, Ohio State can create the separation the market expects without needing much help from turnovers or short fields.

The question for us is whether Illinois can make Sayin work through longer possessions rather than allowing the passing game to dictate the matchup. That battle is the clearest threat to our model’s more restrained view of the margin.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 win over Ball State.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards, including 434 passing and 237 rushing, and converted all of its red-zone opportunities.
Ohio State held Ball State to 165 total yards, including 45 rushing and 120 passing, and allowed conversions on 21.4 percent of third downs.
Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half of the opener.
Running back Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry against Ball State and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Fourteen Ohio State players recorded a reception against Ball State.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in the season opener, and freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards and scored on his first career catch.

opponent_notes.fact: Cornerback Devin Sanchez recorded a 2025 season-high five tackles and a pass breakup against Illinois.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin is Ohio State's returning starting quarterback and entered 2026 with 15 career starts.
Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025, a school and Big Ten single-season record, while throwing for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Sayin led the nation in completion percentage and ranked second nationally in passing efficiency at 177.5 in 2025.
Justyn Martin entered 2026 with six career appearances and no starts.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned eight offensive starters: quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Bo Jackson, wide receivers Jeremiah Smith and Brandon Inniss, tackle Phillip Daniels, center Carson Hinzman, and guards Luke Montgomery and Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
The starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts after the season opener, while Ohio State returned 85.8 percent of its qualifying offensive-line snaps from 2025.
Center Carson Hinzman entered 2026 with 36 career starts, Austin Siereveld with 21, Phillip Daniels with 17 and Luke Montgomery with 17.
Bo Jackson rushed for a team-high 1,090 yards on 179 carries in 2025 and returned as Ohio State's starting running back.
Jeremiah Smith entered 2026 with 171 career receptions, 2,709 receiving yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.

Ohio State added experienced transfer receivers Devin McCuin from UTSA and Kyle Parker from LSU; McCuin had 158 career receptions for 1,793 yards and 17 touchdowns, while Parker had 34 catches for 385 yards and five touchdowns.
Hunter Welcing, a transfer tight end from Northwestern, entered 2026 with 40 career games and 11 starts.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returned three defensive starters from 2025: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters: tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.

Ohio State added defensive transfers James Smith and Qua Russaw from Alabama, John Walker from UCF, Christian Alliegro from Wisconsin, Earl Little Jr. from Florida State and Beau Atkinson from North Carolina.
Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025 and entered 2026 with 9.5 career sacks.
Safety Earl Little Jr. led Florida State with 76 tackles in 2025 before transferring to Ohio State.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro entered 2026 with 127 career tackles and eight sacks.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are offensive coordinator Arthur Smith, defensive coordinator Matt Patricia and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen serves as run game coordinator and offensive line coach, Billy Fessler as pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Matt Guerrieri as pass game coordinator and safeties coach.

offensive_context.fact: Ohio State returned a 3,500-yard passer, a 1,000-yard receiver and a 1,000-yard rusher after having all three in each of the previous two seasons.
Ohio State averaged 39.6 points per game from the start of Ryan Day's head-coaching tenure in 2019 through the 2026 opener.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed 9.3 points and 219.1 total yards per game in 2025, ranking first nationally in scoring and total defense.
The Buckeyes allowed 129.7 passing yards per game in 2025 and 8.73 yards per completion.
From the start of 2024 through the 2026 opener, Ohio State allowed 10.9 points, 235.7 total yards and 148.6 passing yards per game.
Ohio State allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games from the start of 2024 through the 2026 opener, including nine games without allowing a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's only returning specialist starter.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann after the 2025 season.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State entered 2026 with 34 returning letterwinners and 31 lost letterwinners, including 11 returning starters and 11 lost starters.
Ohio State was listed as the 11th-youngest team nationally, fifth-youngest in the Power Four and second-youngest in the Big Ten, with an average age of 19.95.
